items.statement: Most cash profits converted to cash; working capital investment only 5%
items.quote: I'm pretty happy to say that pretty much most of our cash profits have been converte d to cash and if you see the working capital investment is only 5

items.statement: Management expects to be self-sufficient in funding CAPEX from internal accruals without hampering cash flows, maintaining a mix of debt and equity.
items.quote: Self sufficient in doing the CAPEX, but does not hamper the cash flows, we always keep a mix and match of debt and equity because if you see my credit, facilities that T have, I am not using it 100%, that reflects in the credit rating that has been given by CRISIL as well.

items.statement: Management indicates current debt levels around Rs. 400 crore may remain near the same level over the next two years, with only a small potential increase.
items.quote: And going forward if you see after two years the current debt would also be repaid. So it should be near to the same level of 10% highes than what we are today.

items.statement: Management states no equity dilution planned; growth will be funded through internal accruals and existing credit facilities.
items.quote: Not necessarily if the company is having enough CAPEX or cash flows for the CAPEX, we might not take any debt or a small debt maybe.

items.statement: Management states seed production is exempt from income tax, resulting in low tax payments and good cash flows.
items.quote: Seed industry do not have income tax as seed production is exempted from income tax. And you can see major players in the industry are also doing the same.

items.statement: Management confirms a buyback from the open market occurred in the last 15 days.
items.quote: Sir, I have buyback from open market in last 15 days only, but yes, we will take your note.

items.statement: Indorama Ventures acquires 24.9% stake from Blackstone; Blackstone remains largest shareholder and promoter
items.quote: Indorama Ventures Limited, IVL, has entered into a definitive agreement to acquire a 24.9% minority stake in EPL from Blackstone.

items.statement: Blackstone retains half its stake and continues as promoter with majority board representation
items.quote: Blackstone will continue as our largest shareholder and promoter, reaffirming their strong belief in EPL's value creation journey and also its future growth potential.

items.statement: Indorama will not be categorized as promoter and will get one board seat
items.quote: The current plan is that all these 8 continue. So the 4 Blackstone Directors, me and the 3 Independent Directors, and there is provision for a ninth Board seat, and that goes to Indorama, okay

items.statement: No current transactions with Indorama for raw materials or finished goods
items.quote: So we do not have any transactions with Indorama as of today.

items.statement: Share purchase agreement has no call, put option or right of first refusal for either side
items.quote: So the current agreement is only about the 24.9% share sale and there is no further call or put option or ROFR, which is right of first refusal.

items.statement: Receivables at 74 days including solar business, maintained well
items.quote: Receivable this is also under control. You can see 74 days, even including solar. We are maintaining this very well.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 323 crore as of December end
items.quote: Cash, good improvement. You can see $323 crore as net cash position as of December end.

items.statement: Solar business causing longer working capital cycle due to installation, certification and payment process
items.quote: So we are financing this business, and fortunately, KSB has a very good financial standing and strength that we are able to sustain this long working capital cycle.

items.statement: DSO increase of 3-4 days mainly due to solar Kusum business in initial year
items.quote: As I mentioned, this is mainly due to solar because in the initial year or so, maybe, three to four days around.

items.statement: CVC sold majority stake to KKR; KKR to acquire up to 54% equity from CVC and hold 54-77% post open offer; Dr. Ajaikumar remains co-promoter, CVC reclassified as public shareholder
items.quote: Upon completion of the transaction and open offer, KKR is expected to hold an equity stake of between 54-77%, and this is based on what happens in the open offer. I will be also classified as co-promoter.

items.statement: Cash conversion improved from sub-90% to 100% and will be maintained through working capital optimization and asset monetization
items.quote: From a sub-90% last year, we are sequentially going to, are delivering 100% cash conversion to EBITDA and we intend to keep it this way for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Parent AkzoNobel NV proposes to buy the powder coatings business and international research centre from the listed entity, and sell decorative paints IP rights and brands to the listed entity.
items.quote: parent has come back to India entity somewhere in early January asking that they would like to buy out the Powder Coatings business. And at the same time, they would like to buy out the International Research Cent re, which is situated out of Bangalore. And they also proposed that intellectual property along with the brand would be sold to the India

items.statement: Powder coatings business valued at Rs 20.7 billion (24.5x trailing EBITDA) by KPMG and Grant Thornton; R&D centre valued at Rs 579-700 million; decorative IP rights valued at Rs 11.5 billion via royalty relief method.
items.quote: the powder business, it was valued at ₹20.7 billion in a blended source of the market multiple and the disc ounted cash flows for the future investments. And the range came between ₹20.6 billion to ₹20.7 billion. So we chose the highest from that to get us say consideration for the transaction

items.statement: Listed entity will receive net cash inflow of Rs 990 crore pre-tax from the combined transaction (sale of powder coatings and R&D centre minus purchase of decorative IP).
items.quote: So the ₹990 crores inflow into AkzoNobel listed companies, pre-tax?

items.statement: Tax impact estimated at around 14% of the sale consideration for the powder coatings and R&D centre divestment.
items.quote: Taxation impact could be around 14% of the purchase consideration or the sale consideration. Yeah.

items.statement: R&D centre sold is a captive cost centre with 12% markup recharged to Netherlands; powder coatings has three manufacturing sites at Bangalore, Thane and Gwalior with no technology or facility dependency on other businesses.
items.quote: It's a completely captive consumption centre. So it's the cost of the R&D facility which we run in Bangalore. The entire cost gets recharged to the Netherlands pass through. Unidentified Speaker: Pass through is a markup. Rajiv Rajgopal: So the 12% markup is a profit which was realised in the listed

items.statement: Inventory and receivables aging improved except for KTM-related stock buildup
items.quote: Yeah, other than KTM everything is improving. As Prabh has already explained you know, since they are on active recovery mode, so first step will be to liquidate the inventory.

items.statement: Over 17 years since IPO, Redington generated sufficient cash to fund 15% revenue CAGR, pay 40% dividend payout, and reduce debt-equity from 0.7x to 0.22x without raising fresh capital.
items.quote: In this period, no capital got raised. 15% CAGR, we just saw. 40 % dividend is the dividend policy, last 5 years we have paid 20 % from IPO till that time. Third, look at the debt equity, during our IPO the debt equity was 0.7 times and today it is about 0.2, 0.22 times.

items.statement: Management expects working capital days to remain in the 35-40 day range, currently at 35-36 days, which is better than pre-COVID levels of 45+ days.
items.quote: And we had said, our expectation is about 35 to 40 days and we are within that range.

items.statement: Redington uses forward contracts to hedge forex exposure, paying premium built into product pricing, resulting in forex loss of only 5 bps in P&L over the period.
items.quote: But having said that, there are some markets where, I mean forward contracts are not possible. So, in which case, we have different other, other methodologies, the business model could be such that a natural hedging is possible.

items.statement: Receivable provisions at 10 bps and inventory provisions at 6 bps of revenue over 17 years, with maximum combined provision of 30 bps in any year.
items.quote: Our inventory provision is 6 bps, which is 0.06% of revenue. So, together we are talking about a 16-bps charge in P&L for both the risks.

items.statement: Promoter stepped off the board in 2017; Redington has been a fully board-governed company since then with no promoter involvement.
items.quote: We've been a board-governed company for a while now and 2017 the promoter stepped off and we've been a fully board-governed company and we're very fortunate to have a fantastic board.

items.statement: Closing cash balance was $233 million driven by low DSOs of 65 days
items.quote: Our closing cash balance was $233 million, primarily driven by DSOs, which has been one of the lowest from an industry perspective. We closed Q4 at 65 days with both billed and unbilled put together.

items.statement: OCF to EBITDA conversion was 81% on reported basis for full year
items.quote: Significantly our OCF to EBITDA was at a very healthy 75% on an adjusted EBITDA basis. But on a reported basis, it was at close to 81%.

items.statement: Comfortable DSO range going forward is around 70 days
items.quote: Just want to add it that our comfortable range in terms of where our DSOs are going to be is around the 70 mark.

items.statement: Oil business is a cash market with maximum 10 days payment; spices in South India is a 2-3 month credit market
items.quote: Oil is a completely 10 maximum is the 10 days payment. So we don't require more capital for the capex for the oil and we already as I said funds has been sufficient for us for next two years also, next financial year so we don't need further funds actually.

items.statement: Poushtik e-commerce is 100% cash business with no credit; only initial capex needed
items.quote: As you know, if there is no credit in this segment, e-commerce. That is a completely 100% cash. So we don't need much. Only for the start we need a capex. Later on we don't need the capex.

items.statement: Promoters did not participate in the recent rights issue due to lack of capital
items.quote: For the right issue thing, Mr. Rajeev, we have already informed in the letter of offer that promoters are not going to participate in the right issue. So it is their interest and I mean it is because of lack of few capital involved so they could not participate.

items.statement: Groundnut oil plant investment is approximately INR15 crores including working capital
items.quote: So almost, it will be INR15 crores almost, including this working capital.

items.statement: Poushtik marketing budget is INR25 lakhs for first quarter; thereafter profits will fund advertising
items.quote: We have planned the advertisement budget of first quarter of the launches, only INR25 lakhs we are going to launch. So I know it's very less budget to do the marketing, but we are going to do the smart marketing.

items.statement: Company has sufficient funds from October rights issue for next two years; no further fundraising needed
items.quote: We already raised the rights in the October. So we can utilize that fund for our oil also from parallelly. Only the spices segment is quite tricky in actually South India is a huge credit market in completely South India is the same with the spices, not with the other. Oil is a completely 10 maximum is the 10 days payment. So we don't require more capital for the capex for the oil and we already a

items.statement: Board approved a soft loan of INR 125 crores from the promoter family at repo plus 0.5% (~7%) with 15-year tenure and 2-year moratorium to conserve free cash flow for growth capital.
items.quote: To support our further growth strategy and to conserve free cash flow on the books whatever we have, the board has also approved INR125 crores soft loan from the promoter family at a repo plus 0.5 that is approximately 7% with a 15 -year tenure that can be extended and a two -year moratorium that also can be extended offering a flexible penalty-free repayment.

items.statement: IPO proceeds included ~INR 60 crores allocated for an unidentified acquisition, which will be used to fund the majority stake purchase in STATCON Energiaa.
items.quote: The GCP, when we had, when we raised the money for the IPO, already allowed us close to 60 crores for another unidentified acquisition. We are using the money from the IPO and not from anywhere else.

items.statement: STATCON acquisition will be a primary-only transaction funded from IPO proceeds; transaction size not yet disclosed but within the raised amount.
items.quote: The other discussion that has happened at this moment is it will be a primary only transaction.

items.statement: Management announced a partnership with international investors to jointly invest up to 100 million USD over three to five years for PPP project equity requirements.
items.quote: Today we are pleased to announce that we have agreed with international investors to jointly invest up to 100 million USD over the next three to five years.

items.statement: Merger approved with share exchange ratio of 100 Kopran Limited shares for 45 Kopran Laboratories shares
items.quote: The proposed share exchange ratio is 100 fully paid up equity shares of Kopran Limited against 45 fully paid up equity shares of Kopran Laboratories Limited after receiving all the regulatory approvals.
